tasks.prompt: The foundation pour at Maple Court Phase II is set for tomorrow. Heavy rain is forecast all afternoon. What do you do?

options.why: Maybe, maybe not. That's exactly what a conflict check is for.

options.label: Turn them away without explanation
options.why: Cautious, but you don't know yet that there's a real conflict.

tasks.prompt: You realize a brief you filed last week cites a case that was overturned on appeal. Nobody has noticed yet. What do you do?

options.why: Lawyers owe the court candor. Owning it fast limits the damage.

options.detail: Tell her you won't work with someone who wants to lie, and end the meeting
options.why: May be needed if she insists, but talk to her first.

options.detail: Fast and neutral; she can call you with questions if she has any

options.detail: Pros, cons, risks of trial, your recommendation
options.why: The client decides, but they deserve your advice and time to think.

options.why: Doesn't fix the contaminated test set.

options.why: An honest number is the only useful number.

options.label: Refuse and drop the project

options.label: Copy whatever approach a rival lab announced
